dissents.topic: Severity of the README diff (mixed cosmetic + semantic changes)

positions.position: P0 — three-patches-in-one, would refuse in current shape; split into separate diffs
P2 — cosmetic reformat hides a load-bearing signature edit; audit and document
P2 — complected commit, split cosmetic from semantic
P2 — smuggles a public contract change, split or call out explicitly
P2 — formatting churn with one buried semantic change, separate next time
P2 — sprawling reformat unrelated to stated scope, separate the concerns

dissents.topic: Whether resp4 (Content-Length: 1, empty body -> 400) is a sufficient regression test

positions.position: Correct assertion; only nit is the missing comment naming the invariant under test
Test couples example behavior to an undocumented framework promise about bounded_stream; assert directly against bounded_stream instead
Test passes for the wrong reason as easily as the right one; must also assert response body/title
Status-only assertions miss Location header and db.add_thing side-effect postconditions
TESTED-NOT-PROVED — the 400 from 'lie about Content-Length' is indistinguishable from the 400 from 'honest empty body'; the interesting case is not pinned

dissents.topic: How to treat the FAQ PostTest example

positions.position: Add a one-paragraph literate comment stating the three-branch invariant; align with bounded_stream
Strip to header-override only; the worked handler complects three concerns and teaches a bug
Bad taste — redundant `or 0` special-case the framework already handles; fix style
Add a class docstring stating the abstract operation contract; don't hand-roll length checks
Example is contrived — 30+ lines of scaffolding to show one-line header override; reduce to minimum
Folklore-by-example — handler is UNREASONED; either prove the property or don't advertise it

issues.description: README diff bundles unrelated refactors (signature change, stream swap, formatting) into a test-additions PR
issues.detail: The README changes include a StorageError.handle signature reorder (ex, req, resp, params -> req, resp, ex, params), a req.stream -> req.bounded_stream swap, str(code)+reason -> falcon.code_to_http_status, and extensive PEP8 reflow. None of this belongs in a patch titled 'add POST request tests for things_advanced'. Torvalds rates this as a blocker requiring the diff to be split into separate intentional patches; other reviewers (Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, Pike, Dijkstra) flag the same mixing at P2 severity. Either way, the cosmetic churn hides load-bearing edits and makes the patch hard to bisect and review.

issues.description: Silent StorageError.handle signature change in README with no test, news fragment, or rationale
issues.detail: The README example flips StorageError.handle from (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params). This is a real public-contract change for Falcon error handlers. Torvalds calls it a wrong-shape drive-by edit that would break copy-pasters and demands its own patch with justification. Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, Pike, and Dijkstra all flag the same change at P2 — at minimum it must be called out explicitly, with the rationale stated (which Falcon version moved to this ordering, and whether the old form is still supported).

issues.description: req.stream -> req.bounded_stream swap in things_advanced.py is the load-bearing semantic change, undocumented and misdescribed
issues.detail: The one-line change in examples/things_advanced.py from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() is the actual fix — bounded_stream respects Content-Length and won't block on a lying client. All six reviewers flag this. The PR description claims the change 'adds req.content_length to req.stream.read()' which is not what the diff does (Dijkstra, Torvalds, Liskov, Pike). No comment at the call site explains why bounded_stream is preferred or what it guarantees (Knuth, Pike, Hickey, Liskov, Dijkstra). The contract distinction between the two stream ADTs (raw WSGI input vs Content-Length-bounded) is a real substitution boundary that must be named.

issues.description: FAQ example contradicts the things_advanced.py fix and teaches the wrong pattern
issues.detail: The FAQ PostTest handler calls req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0) while the same PR changes things_advanced.py to req.bounded_stream.read() precisely to avoid this pattern. Knuth flags the direct contradiction between the two examples in the same PR. Liskov and Hickey note the handler hand-rolls length checking against req.stream rather than using the bounded_stream ADT the framework already provides — exactly the leaky abstraction the fix elsewhere removes. Pick one idiom (bounded_stream) and state the invariant.

issues.description: FAQ PostTest handler has no stated invariant for its three-branch logic
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post branches on content_length and on whether read returns truthy bytes, producing 200/201/400. The intended invariant ('Content-Length absent or 0 -> 200; declared bytes present -> 201; declared but body empty -> 400') is the whole point of the example and is nowhere stated. Knuth wants a literate-comment paragraph; Liskov wants a class docstring stating the abstract operation contract; Dijkstra calls the handler UNREASONED folklore-by-example. Without the spec written down the example reads as ad-hoc branching that readers will copy.

issues.description: FAQ example is contrived and over-built for what it teaches
issues.detail: Pike: the mechanism being demonstrated (passing headers= to simulate_post) is one line, but it's wrapped in 30+ lines of fixture, resource class, and branching status logic that exist to make the test interesting, not to teach the API. Hickey: the snippet complects header override, empty-body semantics, and Content-Length trust — answering 'how do I override a header' via a handler that itself models a subtle bug. Strip to the minimum that shows the header override, and link separately to the empty-body semantics discussion.

issues.description: FAQ handler contains a redundant special-case that the framework already handles (bad taste)
issues.detail: PostTest checks `req.content_length in (None, 0)` then does `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)`. Torvalds flags that the `or 0` guard is dead code in the else branch because the outer if already excluded None and 0 — write it so the special case disappears, or don't write the special case. The redundancy is also a symptom of the deeper complecting Hickey identifies: declared length, actual bytes, and parse success tangled in one function.

issues.description: resp4 test asserts only a status code that the honest-empty-body path also returns — does not actually pin the regression
issues.detail: Dijkstra: the example handler raises HTTPBadRequest for 'Empty request body' on `if not body:` — the same 400 an honest empty POST produces. The test does not distinguish 'bounded_stream returned empty because body was empty' from 'bounded_stream handled the Content-Length lie correctly' — TESTED-NOT-PROVED. Torvalds: passes for the wrong reason as easily as the right one; must assert the response body/title (Malformed JSON or Empty request body). Hickey: asserts an undocumented framework promise transitively through the example rather than directly against bounded_stream. Liskov: status-only assertions also miss the Location header and db.add_thing side-effect postconditions of the 201 path.

issues.description: PR description does not match the diff
issues.detail: The summary says 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' but the actual change is req.stream -> req.bounded_stream with no argument. Dijkstra notes either the author didn't understand the change or didn't update the description — either way the change was not reasoned about before being written. Torvalds: bad commit messages waste the maintainer's time, fix the description or split the patch.

issues.description: New test lacks a comment naming what regression it guards
issues.detail: tests/test_examples.py resp4 has no docstring or comment explaining the invariant under test. Knuth: two lines of comment ('this guards the bounded_stream change; a regression to req.stream.read() would hang or return empty bytes') would make the test self-documenting and prevent a future maintainer from 'fixing' it by switching back. Hickey wants the same explanation but framed as 'document the framework promise being relied on'.

issues.description: FAQ uses `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` — parenthesized assert antipattern in user-facing docs
issues.detail: assert is a statement, not a function. The parens make it read as a call and risk the well-known `assert(x, y)` pitfall (a 2-tuple is always truthy, so the assertion silently passes). Knuth, Torvalds, Pike, and Dijkstra all flag this as a documentation-quality issue — the FAQ is a copy-paste surface and should model the discipline the framework expects of users. Write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400`.

issues.description: FAQ uses list-of-tuples for headers while the new tests use dicts — two header idioms in one PR
issues.detail: headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),] in the FAQ vs dict form in tests/test_examples.py. Pike: pick the dict form everywhere so the data shape is obvious. Dijkstra: also notes the trailing comma inside the single-element list is harmless but inconsistent with the rest of the codebase. Documentation should model the canonical idiom.

issues.description: Underlying handler still complects 'is there a body' with 'is the body well-formed JSON'
issues.detail: Hickey: JSONTranslator.process_request reads the stream, checks `if not body`, then tries json.loads — three distinct facts (declared length, actual bytes, parseable JSON) tangled in one function with three different error paths. The bug that motivated this PR is a symptom of that tangling. Not blocking for this PR but worth naming because the fix patches a symptom.

issues.description: Test uses magic Authorization 'custom-token' that only works because the example's auth stub returns True
issues.detail: Torvalds: AuthMiddleware._token_is_valid is `return True  # Suuuuuure it's valid...` so any string passes. Fine today, but if the example's auth stub is ever fixed, the tests silently break in a confusing way. A one-line comment in the test ('auth is a stub in the example') would save the next maintainer five minutes.

issues.description: Hardcoded path '/1337/things' and overlapping headers duplicated across new test cases with no shared fixture
issues.detail: Torvalds: not worth a fixture for two cases, but if a third lands it becomes copy-paste sprawl. Pike: the test function now does four unrelated assertions (GET 200, GET 200 again, POST 201, POST 400) in one body — splitting into named tests would make failures more diagnosable. Not a blocker; n is small.

issues.description: Termination/edge-case behavior of bounded_stream with absent Content-Length or chunked encoding not addressed
issues.detail: Knuth: switching from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() changes behavior when Content-Length is absent or when chunked transfer encoding is used. The example adds no comment explaining what bounded_stream guarantees (will not block past the declared body length) and what it does when the header is missing entirely. A one-line literate comment at the call site would make the example pedagogically honest.

issues.description: No towncrier news fragment visible despite checklist claim
issues.detail: Dijkstra: the PR checklist asserts that towncrier news fragments under docs/_newsfragments/ have been added; the diff shows no such file. Either the checklist is incorrect or the fragment was added but not shown — either way the discipline of the checklist depends on it being true. Ticked-but-not-done is worse than not ticked.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converge on one strongest claim: the load-bearing change in this PR is a single line — req.stream.read() becoming req.bounded_stream.read() in examples/things_advanced.py — and it is undocumented, misdescribed in the PR summary, and contradicted by the FAQ example which still teaches the req.stream pattern. The second strongest convergence is that the README diff smuggles a real StorageError.handle signature change and a stream-API swap inside a sprawling cosmetic reformat, mixing semantic and stylistic edits in a patch titled 'add POST tests'. The strongest preserved disagreement is severity of that mixing: Torvalds calls it P0 and would refuse the PR in current shape pending a split, while Knuth, Hickey, Liskov, Pike, and Dijkstra flag the same mixing at P2. A secondary disagreement runs through the resp4 test: Knuth treats it as a correct assertion needing only a comment, while Dijkstra, Torvalds, Hickey, and Liskov argue the status-only assertion does not actually distinguish the lie-about-Content-Length path from the honest-empty-body path and so fails to pin the regression it claims to guard. The panel agrees the test additions are directionally good and the bounded_stream choice is correct, but the framing — PR description, FAQ pattern, README scope, test assertions — is consistently under-specified.
